analysis: The code snippet calls `toArray` on a `Set<Class<?>>` named `interfaceClasses`. The set is populated from `interfaceType.getTypes().interfaces().rawTypes()` and `Serializable.class`. The argument passed to `toArray` is `new Class<?>[interfaceClasses.size()]`, which is a newly allocated array. According to the API documentation, `toArray` throws `NullPointerException` if the specified array is null, and `ArrayStoreException` if the runtime type of the specified array is not a supertype of the runtime type of every element in the set. In this context, the array is explicitly created and cannot be null, so `NullPointerException` is avoided. The array type is `Class<?>[]`, and all elements in the set are `Class<?>` instances (since `rawTypes()` returns `Class<?>` objects), meaning the array type is a supertype of every element's runtime type. Thus, `ArrayStoreException` is also avoided.
remark: No exceptions from `toArray` are thrown in this context. The array is non-null, and its runtime type (`Class<?>[]`) is compatible with all elements (`Class<?>`). Therefore, both declared exceptions are avoided.
